def can_visit_all(start, oases, V):
    n = len(oases)
    water = V
    left = start
    right = start
    # We'll expand range of visited oases
    while left > 0 or right < n - 1:
        # Try to go left if possible
        if left > 0:
            dist = oases[left] - oases[left - 1]
            if water >= dist:
                water -= dist
                left -= 1
                water = V  # refill at oasis
                continue
        # Try to go right if possible
        if right < n - 1:
            dist = oases[right + 1] - oases[right]
            if water >= dist:
                water -= dist
                right += 1
                water = V
                continue
        # If can't move directly, consider jumping
        # Jump halves water, we can jump to any point
        if water > 0:
            # Try to jump to extend reach
            if left > 0:
                dist = oases[left] - oases[left - 1]
                if water >= dist:
                    water = water // 2
                    if water >= dist:
                        water -= dist
                        left -= 1
                        water = V
                        continue
            if right < n - 1:
                dist = oases[right + 1] - oases[right]
                if water >= dist:
                    water = water // 2
                    if water >= dist:
                        water -= dist
                        right += 1
                        water = V
                        continue
        # If still cannot move, fail
        return False
    return True


def main():
    import sys
    input_data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
    if not input_data:

import sys

def can_from_leftmost(xs, V):
    n = len(xs)
    if n <= 1:
        return True

    # State after covering a prefix and standing at its rightmost oasis:
    # walk = reachable with exact walking only
    # jump = reachable if we may have used one jump at some time before/at now
    walk = V
    jump = V / 2.0

    for i in range(n - 1):
        d = xs[i + 1] - xs[i]

        # From previous states, after reaching next oasis and refilling:
        new_walk = walk - d
        new_jump = max(jump - d, walk / 2.0)

        if new_walk < 0 and new_jump < 0:
            return False

        walk = min(V, new_walk) if new_walk >= 0 else -1.0
        jump = min(V, new_jump) if new_jump >= 0 else -1.0

    return True

def solve():
    data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
    if not data:
        return

    it = iter(data)
    N = int(next(it))
    V = int(next(it))
    xs = [int(next(it)) for _ in range(N)]
    xs.sort()

    # Starting from an interior oasis is always no harder than starting from
    # one of the extremes, because you can first move to one side and then
    # traverse to the other with refills on the way.
    # So all starts are possible iff both extreme starts are possible.
    ok_left = can_from_leftmost(xs, V)
    ok_right = can_from_leftmost([-x for x in reversed(xs)], V)

    print("Yes" if ok_left and ok_right else "No")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    solve()
